findings.title: A covered repo passed in URL or other non-canonical form silently gets the platform PAT.
findings.body: `normalize_repo` returns None for `https://github.com/acme/app`, `git@github.com:acme/app.git`, `acme/app/` and similar strings. `token_for_repo` then returns None, which means "not covered", and `resolve_github_token` falls back to the platform PAT. So if a caller passes a covered repo as a clone URL (a common shape in this codebase's git paths), it gets the wide-reach platform PAT instead of the scoped token. FR-4 exists to rule that out, and nothing signals that it happened. Fix: either canonicalize the URL forms to `owner/repo` before validating, or treat an unparseable repo as an error (raise `GithubTokenUnavailable` or `ValueError`) whenever a provider is registered, so it never falls through to the PAT.

held.title: A wall-clock bound in a unit test can fail on a slow or loaded CI runner.
held.body: The bounded pattern still backtracks up to about 512 characters at each of the 16,000 `ghs_` start positions, roughly 8M regex steps, and `sanitize_text` also runs every other pattern. On a shared CI runner this can come close to the 0.5 s limit and fail intermittently. The same test is in `test_credential_sanitizer_agent.py`. Consider a looser bound, or compare against a baseline measured in the same test run.
